title_or_table: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE), counties, people under 65, all incomes, both sexes, all races
table_id: SAHIE timeseries, AGECAT=1, IPRCAT=0, SEXCAT=0, RACECAT=0, time=2024
geography: 3144 counties and county equivalents in the 50 states and DC, with each county's Census region
unit: uninsured_pct in percent, with its 90 percent margin of error in percentage points; counts in people
vintage: SAHIE 2024 release (the latest year in the data API on November 11, 2026)
qualification: Model-based estimates that combine survey and administrative data; small counties carry wide margins of error, so a box plot shows spread and no single county is ranked. Each county counts once, whatever its population, so the box describes counties, not people, and the note under the chart says so
notes: 1 margin-of-error cells read "<0.1" in the source and are left empty here
classes [634, 1144, 753, 612], none 1; intervals crossing a break 1705, two 0; pairs two classes apart within margin 0

uninsured_class.description: class 1 to 4 by the breaks; empty with no estimate

breaks_crossed.description: breaks inside the 90 percent interval; empty with no margin

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Health Insurance Estimates, people under 65 without health insurance, 2024, counties in the 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Model-based estimates; small counties carry wide margins of error.
derivation: Each county's class by breaks at [8.0, 12.0, 16.0] percent (Rule 14.9: every inner class at least as wide as the widest published margin, 3.3 points) and the count of breaks inside its 90 percent interval; rows in the source file's geoid order (production test, simulated designer, sahie_classes_derive.py)
